conditional_orbit.formula: a=(G*M*(P/(2*pi))**2)**(1/3); m*sin(i)=c*A*M/a; small companion and circular orbit

entries.summary: Solitary millisecond pulsar in Bootes. Spin 5.79 ms (173 Hz). Detected in Arecibo observations dated 1998-01-19; detailed paper in 2007.
entries.scope: Published estimates: distance about 1.2 kpc (3,900 light-years), dispersion-based; characteristic spin-down age about 8 Gyr, not measured chronological age.

entries.summary: Lorimer et al. (2007) searched three years of timing data and found no significant periodic companions.
entries.scope: Smaller bodies below the published sensitivity were not excluded. New to Recherche does not mean never searched.

entries.summary: Behrens et al. (2020), NG11: no planets detected. J1453+1902 Table 1 reports 8.39 lunar masses at a 100-day period.
entries.scope: Earlier NG11 observations overlap later NG15 coverage. Sensitivity definition differs from our conditional candidate mass estimate.

entries.summary: NG15: 122 TOAs and 122 paired DM measurements, July 2013 to July 2020. Peak 118.4273 days, 1.5262 us, statistic 34.9142 versus frozen 26.8265.
entries.scope: Independent likelihood agrees. Null reduced chi-square 1.2573, upper-tail p=0.0147. Broad noise flag did not fire; complete noise adequacy is not established.

entries.summary: If all signal is a circular orbit about a 1.4-solar-mass pulsar: separation 0.5280 AU; m sin(i) 0.0027003 Earth masses (about 0.22 lunar masses).
entries.scope: Kepler law: a=[G M (P/2pi)^2]^(1/3); m sin(i) approx c A M/a. Unknown inclination raises true mass. Not a measured planet mass, radius, composition or discovery.

entries.summary: Inspect saved timing data and the 118-day fit. Refine period locally with uncertainty and compare observing-window aliases, including the 121.75-day annual third harmonic.
entries.scope: Use one predeclared local interval. Remove one observing epoch at a time to identify domination by a few measurements. Preserve original search and threshold.

entries.summary: Check early versus late epochs and 430 MHz versus L-band measurements for compatible phase and timing amplitude. Available: 49 TOAs at 430 MHz, 73 at L-band, all Arecibo/PUPPI.
entries.scope: Use correct paired TOA/DM rows and subset covariance; prune empty nuisance columns. Lower subset sensitivity can make a non-detection inconclusive. All data already entered discovery.

entries.summary: Compare a small fixed set of alternative noise/dispersion models with and without the candidate. Run one bounded null and signal-injection exercise on actual sampling.
entries.scope: Released model has white-noise and DM terms but no red-noise component. Carry model fitting/selection through simulations; do not recycle the original fixed-noise significance for changed models. Frequency-dependent delays are a specific alternative.

entries.summary: If internal checks retain the signal, examine the downloaded narrowband reduction and look for genuinely nonoverlapping public epochs or another observatory.
entries.scope: Narrowband is a different reduction of shared observations, not independent confirmation. New data availability is unverified. Outcome: rejected, inconclusive, or retained candidate.
